name: Mississippi

cover_rules: MS 340: Plant the cover crop as early as possible and terminate as late as practical (late vegetative stage or later) to maximize biomass.
MS 340: Do not mechanically harvest cover crop biomass. Allow residues to remain on the surface following termination.

cover.name: Crimson Clover
cover.note: MS 512: Plant Sept.-Oct., 1/4 inch deep. Best on fertile, well drained soils.

cover.name: Arrowleaf Clover
cover.note: MS 512: Plant Sept.-Oct., 1/4 inch deep. Not suited to light textured, droughty soils.

cover.name: Ball Clover
cover.note: MS 512: Plant Sept.-Oct., 1/4-1/2 inch deep. Suited to wetter and lighter textured soils.

cover.name: Vetch
cover.note: MS 512: Plant Sept.-Oct., 1/2 inch deep. Listed as Hairy of Wooly Pod Vetch.

cover.name: White Clover
cover.note: MS 512: Plant Sept.-Oct., 1/4 inch deep. Adapted to a wide range of soils.

cover.name: Red Clover
cover.note: MS 512: Plant Sept.-Oct., 1/4 inch deep. Needs fertile, moderately well drained soils.

cover.name: Wild Winter Peas
cover.note: MS 512: Plant Sept.-Oct., 1/4 inch deep. Not adapted to light and sandy soils.

cover.name: Partridge Pea
cover.note: MS 512: Plant March-May, 1/2 inch deep. Grows on practically all soils in Mississippi.

coverPlant.text: MS 512: Plant winter clovers and vetch Sept.-Oct.

seedWin.text: MS 512: Plant native grasses such as Big Bluestem, Switchgrass and Indiangrass March-May.
MS 512: Plant Bahiagrass and Common Bermudagrass March-May.
MS 512: Plant Tall Fescue Sept.- Nov.
